text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — autoscaler ceiling hit for gpu-pool-3 in eu-west-1. queue_length=940, avg_latency=1.8s, throttle_rate=40%

sam (oncall): I'm on it. seeing sustained enqueue from realtime-batches. autoscaler logs show 'max_node_count reached'.

taylor: confirming — HPA tried to scale but nodepool max=48. current=48, pending_pods=62. Kubernetes events: FailedScheduling.

priya: any customers impacted?

customer-success: we have two customers reporting 500s and slow responses on embedding jobs started ~08:45 UTC. CS is triaging and reaching out.

mike: metrics check: GPU utilization is 93% across pool, queue growth ~+300/min over last 10m. Fallback model configured but traffic not routed because model variant not compatible with some requests.

sam (oncall): quick mitigation plan: (1) request temporary nodepool max increase from infra quota owners, (2) enable routing to cpu-backup for non-latency-critical jobs, (3) apply aggressive prefix caching for repeated prompts. who can raise the cap?

jessica: I can request manual cap bump via infra-runbook. Need approval from infra-ops and cost-owner. pinging @ops-bot to open a request.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7321: "Emergency nodepool capacity increase for gpu-pool-3". Approvals required: infra-ops, finance-ops. Approver list: @taylor, @maria-finance (auto CC).

priya: while approvals are in flight, sam — can you flip routing for non-realtime endpoints to the smaller fp16-quant variants? That should relieve some GPU pressure.

sam (oncall): doing it now. Applying traffic policy change:
```
# service routing change
redwoodctl route update realtime --fallback-model cpu-backup --percent-traffic 25
```

sam (oncall): routing change applied. monitoring queue.

mike: good call. observed immediate drop in enqueue rate for gpu jobs by ~18%. latency for critical realtime unchanged but backlog still large.

jessica: infra-ops approved. finance sign-off pending but infra-ops gave green. ops-bot: escalate to platform-admin for manual override?

ops-bot: platform-admin notified. Manual override window requested: +12 nodes for gpu-pool-3. Command to execute (requires platform-admin credentials):
```
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-pool-3 --cluster=redwood-prod-eu --max-nodes=60 --region=eu-west1
```

sam (oncall): @mike standby to validate after resize.

platform-admin (via jessica): executing now. ETA ~4m.

incident-bot: Deploy job started: infra/resize-gpu-pool-3 #4582. logs: attaching...

platform-admin (via jessica): nodes are coming up. kube nodes registering... current=52 -> 56 -> 60.

mike: kube shows new nodes Ready. kube-scheduler is placing pending pods. pending_pods dropped from 62 to 3. Queue drained ~75% in 6m.

sam (oncall): verifying customer impact — CS reports some recovery. Still monitoring for retries and failed jobs.

customer-success: customers A and B report retries cleared and ok for most earlier jobs. One long-running batch failed and needs manual resubmit. CS will coordinate.

priya: we should also temporarily relax token-level rate limiter for background batch endpoints to speed drain. Sam — do you want me to patch limiter?

sam (oncall): yes, increase batch concurrency by +2 per tenant for 10 minutes. Applying:
```
redwoodctl limits set batch_concurrency --delta=2 --duration=10m
```

sam (oncall): applied. monitoring.

mike: after all changes, avg queue < 120, throttle_rate down to 6%, latency back to 1.05s. Good recovery.

jessica: logging notes: manual cap raise +12 nodes, routing fallback enabled (25% to cpu-backup), rate limiter bump for 10m. We need postmortem: why autoscaler didn't provision earlier? check scale policy, pod anti-affinity, and quota headroom.

sam (oncall): agreed. I'll own the immediate postmortem. action items:
- sam: collect autoscaler logs, HPA events, and pod scheduling failures (due EOD).
- taylor: review nodepool scale policy and suggest changes to max_node_count and surge config.
- priya: check routing rules to ensure fallback variants are allowed for all endpoints or add graceful degradation.
- jessica: document infra override steps and approvals for future emergency windows.

mike: one more note — several pods stuck with affinity to local-ssd label which limited packing. Need to verify node labels and scheduling constraints.

sam (oncall): making a short incident summary for status page and customers. Draft: "We experienced a temporary capacity ceiling in eu-west-1 GPU pool causing queue growth and throttling for embedding and batch jobs. We performed a manual nodepool capacity increase and enabled fallback routing and rate limiter adjustments. Service is recovered; continued checks ongoing. Full postmortem to follow."

customer-success: sending that to impacted customers now. will update on any follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to 'mitigated' by sam at 08:59 UTC. Open actions assigned.

sam (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll kick off the postmortem doc and link it here when ready. tagging for follow-up: @taylor, @priya, @jessica, @mike.

jessica: closing note — keep this channel for postmortem comments. If we need to roll back the node cap after stabilization, we should coordinate a scheduled window.

sam (oncall): ACK. moving to follow-up phase.
